item.title: Remote Adiabatic Controlled-Z Gate between Distant Superconducting Qubits
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Coaxial cable mediating multi-mode ZZ interaction achieves remote adiabatic controlled-Z gate with optimized infidelity of 4.71×10−7 and 376.7 ns duration for 30-cm cable length without tunable couplers.

Grade 0.442 · 2.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Si-Yu Xu, Yi-Rong Jin, Wen-Gang Zhang, Hai-Feng Yu

Figure

Infidelity mapped against both qubit working frequencies, showing a minimum of 4.71×10−7 at $(4.6390, 4.5112)$ GHz. Panels also display infidelity under ±0.5 MHz frequency drift and performance across cable lengths within 30.00±0.10 cm.

Asks

Can an adiabatic CZ gate be realized across a remote multi-mode coaxial cable coupling architecture with low leakage and high-fidelity conditional phase accumulation?

But

Numerical simulation assuming zero decoherence. Ten standing-wave cable modes included.

Tools

time-dependent Hamiltonian evolution · multi-mode standing-wave coaxial cable model · virtual-Z phase correction · transmon frequency tuning

Abstract

Direct entangling gates between spatially separated qubits are a key capability for modular quantum computing. They enable nonlocal quantum circuits to be executed across different processor modules, thereby alleviating single-chip scaling constraints and expanding the effective connectivity of the system. Here, we propose and numerically investigate a remote adiabatic controlled-Z gate between two frequency-tunable superconducting qubits connected by a multi-mode coaxial cable. The cable-mediated interaction enables the gate to be implemented without additional tunable couplers, preserving a simple circuit architecture. For a 30-cm cable, simulations incorporating ten standing-wave modes yield an optimized gate infidelity of 4.71×10⁻⁷ with a duration of 376.7 ns in the absence of decoherence. The gate maintains high fidelity under qubit-frequency fluctuations and millimeter-scale cable-length variations. Calculations for 50- and 100-cm cable situations demonstrate its potential for even larger cryogenic systems. These results provide a promising approach to extending high-fidelity quantum operations beyond individual chips and toward scalable, interconnected superconducting quantum processors.

item.title: A Programmable Rydberg Quantum Bus for Nonlocal Connectivity
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Dispersive Rydberg atom chains act as coherent quantum buses to mediate effective quasi-all-to-all interactions between data units via virtual excitations, analytically derived using Green's-function continued fractions.

Grade 0.426 · 2.3σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · X. Jin, F. Yang, Weibin Li, X. Q. Shao

Figure

Population dynamics of data units coupled to a nine-atom Rydberg chain across single, double, and triple excitation manifolds, plotted against dimensionless time for V/J=40 and Δ/J=80.

Asks

Can a Rydberg atom array provide a stationary quantum bus to mediate coherent nonlocal connectivity between distant data units?

But

Off-resonant dispersive regime with Jμ≪mink⁡|Ek|; validated with Gaussian positional uncertainty σ=0.02 μm and Rydberg lifetimes up to T=77 K.

Tools

Green's function continued-fraction method · Feshbach partitioning · Monte Carlo wavefunction trajectories · Floquet engineering

Abstract

Scalable quantum networks require processing nodes with flexible internal connectivity, yet neutral-atom architectures remain constrained by the strong spatial dependence of native Rydberg interactions. Here we show that a Rydberg atom chain can act as a coherent quantum bus, converting a locally connected one-dimensional architecture into an effectively nonlocal interaction network. Virtual excitations in the dispersive regime mediate controllable interactions between spatially separated data units, which we derive analytically using a Green's-function continued-fraction method. The resulting mechanism is not restricted to single-excitation dynamics and supports several distinct functionalities, including Floquet-engineered chiral transport, remote entanglement of mechanical oscillators, and destructive interference for selectively suppressing unwanted dipole exchange. Simulations incorporating full long-range Rydberg interactions, atomic position fluctuations, and finite Rydberg-state lifetimes show that the mediated dynamics remain robust under experimentally relevant conditions. These results establish Rydberg chains as programmable coherent mediators for extending the internal connectivity of neutral-atom quantum nodes toward quasi-all-to-all coupling, providing a hardware-level route toward scalable and reconfigurable quantum-network architectures.

item.title: Optical Quantum Computing
item.description:
Pay dirt review — Surveys discrete- and continuous-variable optical quantum computing architectures, measurement-based cluster-state models, and non-universal algorithms (boson sampling, VQEs, QML).

Grade 0.420 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Circuit quantum electrodynamics” · Hamza Hasnaoui, Leonardo Limongi, Taira Giordani, Beatrice Polacchi, Alberto Quaranta, Martino Bernard, Fabio Sciarrino, Mirko Lobino

Figure

Taxonomy mapping discrete-variable and continuous-variable universal optical quantum computing models alongside non-universal photonic applications.

Asks

How do optical encoding schemes and computing architectures compare across universal and non-universal quantum platforms?

But

Photonic scaling is constrained by weak single-photon nonlinearities, probabilistic gate generation, and optical propagation losses.

Tools

integrated photonics · continuous-variable squeeze states · discrete-variable cluster states · linear optical interferometry

Abstract

Under the label of optical quantum computing, there are a variety of protocols and experiments that use the quantum properties of light to achieve a computational advantage over classical computing machines. In this review, we describe some of the main implementations, which differ in the type of encoding and in how the computation is performed, whether using gates or cluster states. For each protocol, we describe advantages and challenges with an overview of the experimental results obtained, summarized in tables. Because of the great relevance achieved in this field, there is a section dedicated to non-universal quantum computation with photons, where boson sampling, variational quantum eigensolvers, and quantum machine learning applications are described. The aim is to give the reader the broadest overview of the applications where photons and their quantum properties play a key role in computation.

item.title: Entropy spectroscopy of a tunable two-site Hubbard molecule
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Measured total thermodynamic entropy of a tunable two-site Hubbard molecule across the transition from isolated dots to a merged single dot via single-charge-sensor spectroscopy, resolving thermal suppression of antibonding and triplet states as interdot tunneling increases.

Grade 0.417 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Uhjin Kim, Seokyeong Lee, Gibum Yun, Dongsung T. Park, Soobeom Choi, Sangwoo Jeong, Donghoon Kim, V. Umansky, Yunchul Chung, Hyoungsoon Choi, H. -S. Sim, Hyung Kook Choi

Asks

Which microscopic orbital and spin states remain thermally active in a two-site Hubbard system as tunneling competes with interactions?

Before

Charge-based entropy readout was established only for single quantum dots.

But

Requires shifting both dot levels simultaneously at fixed detuning.

Tools

GaAs/AlGaAs double quantum dot · single-charge-sensor entropy spectroscopy · two-site Hubbard model

Abstract

Determining which microscopic states remain thermally active when tunneling and interactions compete is a central question in Hubbard physics. Here we develop an entropy measurement protocol for a double quantum dot, extending the charge-based approach established for a single dot, and measure the total entropy of a tunable two-site Hubbard molecule realized in a GaAs double dot. By shifting both dot levels together at fixed detuning, the entropy is correctly probed with only a single charge sensor. As interdot tunneling increases, the system evolves from two atomic-like dots through hybridized molecular states to a merged single dot. Across this evolution, the entropy decreases as tunnel-induced energy splitting exceeds the thermal energy and suppresses the occupation of higher-energy states. The measurements resolve the diminishing contribution of antibonding states and the changing thermal contributions of hybridized singlet and triplet states, in quantitative agreement with a two-site Hubbard model. By distinguishing states with the same charge configuration but different orbital and spin content, entropy reveals how tunneling and interactions determine the thermally active states of the minimal Hubbard system.

item.title: Unconventional linear transverse exciton transport in valley-layer coupling two-dimensional materials
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Perpendicular electric field E⟂ tunes exciton-dispersion anisotropy to produce linear transverse exciton transport in monolayer and twisted bilayer TiSiCO, with bilayer transverse conductivities reaching several 1/h at 100K.

Grade 0.415 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Ci Li

Figure

Twist angle θ versus layer-resolved transverse exciton conductivities σHsys, σtrasys,AS, and σtrasys,S at E⟂=−2eV/nm and E⟂=0eV/nm (T=100K). Shows competition between the layer counterflow Hall response and dispersion-anisotropy-induced components.

Asks

Can perpendicular electric fields in valley-layer-coupled 2D materials control exciton dispersion anisotropy to generate and tune linear transverse exciton transport?

But

Zero-Berry-curvature limit; neglects side-jump and skew-scattering high-temperature disorder processes.

Tools

Effective exciton Hamiltonian · Semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory · Relaxation-time approximation · First-principles tight-binding parameters

Abstract

Valley-layer coupling (VLC) two-dimensional (2D) materials define a distinct class of quantum systems in which valleys are related by crystal, rather than time-reversal (T) symmetry, enabling gate-controlled valley-contrasted layer polarization. Here we extend this concept to excitons. Using TiSiCo as a prototype VLC material, we show that a perpendicular electric field E_⊥ controls exciton- dispersion anisotropy and thereby generates unconventional linear transverse exciton transport in both monolayer and twisted bilayer structures. In the monolayer, this response is characterized by anisotropy-induced transverse conductivities, arising from the antisymmetric combination of diagonal elements in the conductivity tensor and strongly tunable by E_⊥. In the twisted bilayer, symmetry additionally permits transverse responses from the symmetric part of the conductivity tensor. Since intralayer excitons in different layers are connected by the Förster coupling, these symmetric and antisymmetric responses coexist and compete with the recently proposed T-even layer Hall and Nernst exciton counterflow. This interplay is highly tunable by twisted angle, temperature, and the direction of the in-plane driving force, providing a route to disentangle distinct transverse exciton transport signals experimentally. Our results establish E_⊥ as a powerful knob for controlling exciton transport via VLC and identify VLC 2D materials as a promising platform for engineered excitonic phenomena.

item.title: Giant-atom-mediated photon blockade
item.description:
Pay dirt new result — Multipoint coupling of giant atom provides additional destructive interference paths, enabling simultaneous unconventional photon blockade in two and three coupled cavities with driven first cavity. Point-atom configuration cannot produce simultaneous unconventional photon blockade.

Grade 0.415 · 2.2σ above the day's baseline · matched “Circuit quantum electrodynamics” · C. Cui, W. Y. Hu, Y. Q. Ji, H. T. Cui, Yan-Hui Zhou, H. Z. Shen

Figure

log10go(2)(0) in a three-cavity system driven at cavity a1 versus coupling phase θ. Shows simultaneous dips to minimum values in all three cavities at θopt=1.2732π and θopt=0.4456π.

Asks

Can multipoint coupling of a giant atom enable simultaneous unconventional photon blockade across multiple coupled cavities?

But

Weak driving regime (F≪κ), equal cavity and atomic dissipations κ1=κ2=κ3=γ≡κ, theoretical model without experimental verification.

Tools

Lindblad master equation · effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian · few-photon state truncation

Abstract

Photon blockade is a phenomenon where the presence of system nonlinearity causes the output to consist of single photons, which has been extensively studied in point atom systems, but it is barely explored in giant atom ones. In this paper, we propose giant atom-mediated photon blockade scheme based on two cavities and three cavities systems with driving field applied to the first cavity. We show that simultaneous unconventional photon blockades (UPBs) can not occur in the point atom system (the atom coupling only to the leftmost cavity) due to there always existing a cavity to have a single path. In contrast, the spatially extended nature of giant atom enables coupling to multiple cavities and allows for the introduction of a phase and coupling strength. Consequently, simultaneous UPBs in multiple cavities can be obtained due to the multipath destructive interference. Moreover, by manipulating the detuning, we observe simultaneous conventional photon blockades (CPBs) in multiple cavities. Finally, we study simultaneous two-photon blockades (2PBs) in point atom multiple cavities system.

item.title: Ancilla-assisted dark-state quantum gates in ultracold polar molecules
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Two-qubit and multi-qubit controlled-phase gates C(φ) can be implemented in optically trapped polar molecules via an ancilla-assisted dark-state mechanism driven solely by two smooth adiabatic microwave π pulses on the ancilla.

Grade 0.411 · 2.1σ above the day's baseline · matched “transmon and fluxonium coherence, single- and two-qubit gate fidelity” · Yan Lu, Xiao-Feng Shi

Figure

Gate infidelity log10⁡(1−F) of the ancilla-assisted CZ gate as a function of the microwave field polarization impurity parameters ς0 and ς.

Asks

How can high-fidelity entangling quantum gates be realized in optically trapped polar molecules without suffering from motional decoherence or Rydberg-state decay?

But

Theoretical and numerical simulation; assumes zero rotational Zeeman effect or weak rotational Zeeman effect relative to nuclear spin Zeeman effect (evaluated for 23Na133Cs at B=2 G); requires specific tweezer alignment to suppress inter-data molecule DDI.

Tools

dipole-dipole interaction (DDI) · adiabatic dark-state evolution · microwave driving · optical tweezer geometry optimization · quantized motional coupling analysis

Abstract

High-fidelity entangling gates are useful for circuit-based quantum computing, yet their realization in a scalable platform is challenging. Optically trapped ultracold polar molecules offer a potentially scalable platform. Here, we introduce a two-qubit molecular entangling gate via a novel ancilla-assisted dark-state mechanism, where high fidelity is achievable. In particular, we find that by using appropriate qubit states for the ancilla and the data qubits, dark states can appear, and entanglement can emerge by driving the ancilla only. It is also feasible to extend the two-qubit gate to a multi-qubit gate via the same dark-state mechanism.

item.title: Chiral classical and quantum acoustics with hole-spin qubits
item.description:
Pay dirt theory — Counterpropagating surface acoustic waves show gate-tunable spin-acoustic chirality up to χ=0.996, yielding a 470-fold transition-strength contrast that enables bichromatic coherence protection with T2,2∗=167 μs (up from T2∗=7.19 μs).

Grade 0.406 · 2.0σ above the day's baseline · matched “Semiconductor spin qubits” · Zhanning Wang, Yongtao Li, Nelson E. Rivas, Gonzalo García, Irene Castro, Rubén Seoane Souto, Daniel Ramos, José C. Abadillo-Uriel

Figure

Timestamp-corrected conditional Bell-state fidelity FBellcond plotted against magnetic-field orientation θB and relative qubit displacement s=2Δx/λPnC. High-fidelity entanglement ridges broaden when acoustic chirality suppresses spatial standing-wave interference nodes.

Asks

How do counterpropagating Rayleigh surface acoustic waves couple to gate-defined hole-spin qubits, and can their directional response be controlled electrostatically?

But

Simulations assume planar Ge quantum well, weak-coupling regime with local defect-mode coupling g0/2π∼1 kHz, ideal unit phonon-detection efficiency, zero dark counts, and zero reset time.

Tools

Six-band Luttinger-Kohn Hamiltonian · Bir-Pikus strain theory · 3D piezoelectric finite-element method (FEM) · Master equation simulation

Abstract

Gate-defined hole spins combine strong spin-orbit coupling with exceptional strain sensitivity, making surface acoustic waves a natural route to remote, phase-coherent control. We show that counterpropagating surface acoustic waves can differ in coupling strength and in whether they predominantly drive spin rotations or modulate the qubit frequency. We call the transverse transition-strength imbalance spin-acoustic chirality and show that it is tunable through gate-controlled reshaping of the dot confinement. Combining a multiband Luttinger-Kohn Hamiltonian with the Bir-Pikus description of strain and 3D piezoelectric finite-element simulations, we obtain the acoustic g-matrix modulation governing coherent SAW driving. Quantizing the same strain-mediated interaction yields the corresponding single-phonon coupling, and a generalized anisotropic Rabi interaction with co-rotating, counter-rotating, and longitudinal components, linking classical chirality to quantum anisotropy and directional one-phonon emission. Magnetic field orientation and dot shape tune the acoustic chirality and operator selectivity. We illustrate this framework through bichromatic coherence protection and phonon-mediated heralded Bell-state initialization.
